one_month_reasoning: The window (to 2026-11-01) contains Q3 2026 earnings, expected around Oct 27-29 (third-party calendar estimate Oct 29), and the Oct 27-28 FOMC meeting. Q3 guide is $210-216M revenue / $0.75-0.82 non-GAAP EPS; Rambus has beaten its guide in Q2, but the April print showed the stock can fall ~23% on a modest miss plus supply-risk commentary, so the earnings reaction is two-sided and fat-tailed. The key item is Q4 product guidance and any comment on DRAM/RDIMM supply limiting module units into 2027. On macro, Polymarket (Fed Decision in October, ~$24.2M volume, read 2026-10-02) prices ~82.5% hold and ~17.5% a 25bp hike, a mild tail risk for high-multiple semis. After a ~30% rally off the August lows, short-term momentum is positive but reversal risk is high. I center the distribution slightly above spot ($112.5) and use a monthly log sigma of about 0.18. That is above RMBS's long-run monthly 0.147 because earnings fall in the window, and below 80%/3.5=0.23 because the 80% realized figure includes the extreme Apr-Jul 2026 swings.

fair_value.method: Blend of 28x estimated 2028 EPS ($4.40, built from 2027 consensus $3.72 growing ~18%) = $123, 30x 2027 consensus EPS $3.72 = $112, and a 20% haircut to the ~$148 consensus analyst target = $118. Weights 50/35/15 give about $118 for the 12-month fair value.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: 2028E EPS $4.40 x 28x forward multiple (the market in Oct 2027 prices the next year)

inputs_detail.derivation: 2027 consensus $3.72 grown ~18%. That is below the 22.6% 2027 consensus growth because TrendForce sees 2027 RDIMM bit supply growth of only 15-20%, which caps unit growth for interface chips. The proprietary model in [16] has a 4% 2028 growth rate, so I treat 18% as base, not bull.

Forward P/E has ranged ~24x (July 2026 trough, [7]) to ~44x (Aug 2026) and ~57x a year earlier ([8]); the 12-month average P/E was ~41x ([9]). Growth slows toward the high teens as the shortage limits units, so I use a multiple near the low end of the recent range.
Midpoint between the 24x trough and the 44x Aug-2026 forward P/E, lowered slightly for the DOJ probe overhang ([4],[5]).

Sell-side targets on RMBS have repeatedly overshot. For example, the stock fell from $174 to $83 within weeks in 2026 while targets stayed near $149 ([7],[2]). A 20% haircut is about one-half of a 1-sigma annual move from the price history ([10]).

bear.story: The DRAM/RDIMM shortage caps module units in 2027. Rambus is unit-leveraged and cannot pass on price ([2],[11]), so product revenue growth stalls and 2027 EPS falls to ~$3.2. The DOJ criminal antitrust probe also escalates or a Fed hike compresses semi multiples, and the stock rerates to ~22x, revisiting the March 2026 low area ($78) and lower.

base.story: Rambus keeps beating its guide modestly. 2027 EPS lands near $3.7 and the market prices 2028E of ~$4.4 at ~27-28x. The DOJ probe stays unresolved but quiet, and the stock grinds toward fair value with typical RMBS volatility.

bull.story: AI inference server builds, MRDIMM/companion-chip content gains and higher royalties push 2027 EPS above $4.2. The multiple returns to the ~40x seen in Aug 2026, retaking the June 2026 high of $174.

thesis_break_reason: $70 is ~10% below the 52-week low ($77.89, March 2026) and ~19x 2027 consensus EPS, a multiple RMBS has not traded at since its AI rerating. A trade there would most likely mean earnings are being cut: memory-supply-driven unit losses, share loss in DDR5 RCD/PMIC, or a DOJ indictment or fine. Ordinary volatility has not taken the stock there in 2026 despite 80% realized vol.

reasoning: Anchor (base rates): from 20 years of RMBS monthly closes (2006-2026, 228 overlapping 12-month windows), the 12-month log-return sd is ~0.45. Median 12-month return is +10%, the 5th/95th percentiles are -60%/+118%, and P(>=1.0x)=0.65, P(>=1.5x)=0.26, P(>=2x)=0.07, P(<0.5x)=0.07. Conditioning on the stock sitting >25% below its trailing-12-month high (as now: $112 vs $174 high) gives 43 cases with a median +63% but a wide 10th percentile of -56%, which supports mean reversion with fat tails. These are overlapping windows and many come from the 2009-2013 and 2023-2025 rebounds, so I give them only modest weight. The 2026 realized vol of 80% is a regime outlier driven by the April -23% post-earnings drop, the June legal and sector selloff, and a ~$174-to-$83 round trip. I use sigma ~0.50 for 12 months, between long-run and current. Center: the fair value of ~$118 sits about 5% above spot; blended with the historical positive drift and offset by known left-tail events (DOJ probe, a shortage that hurts a unit-leveraged business, and Polymarket pricing ~96% no Fed cuts in 2026 with 17.5% odds of an October hike), I set the median at ~$116. Polymarket's US recession market is only 7.5% by end-2026, so macro recession is not the main risk. The ladder is a lognormal (median 116, sigma 0.50) with the far right tail (2x+) trimmed toward the empirical 7% and a slightly fatter far-left tail. The scenario mean (~$121) is consistent. Research limits: Twelve Data estimates were paywalled, so 2027 consensus comes from stockanalysis.com. The Polymarket figures come from the public gamma API on 2026-10-02 (US recession by end of 2026: 7.5% yes, $2.24M volume; Fed Decision in October: 82.5% hold / 17.5% +25bp, $24.2M volume; How many Fed cuts in 2026: 96% zero, $53.8M volume). I found no prediction market specific to Rambus, the DOJ probe or chip tariffs.
